title: AMC AMX Engines by Year (1968–1980)
description: Every factory engine in the AMC AMX by year: the 1968–1970 two-seater's 290, 343, 360 and 390 V8s, and the 1977–1980 Hornet, Concord and Spirit AMX.
intro: AMC used the AMX name on a two-seat sports car from 1968 to 1970 and on sporty versions of the Hornet, Concord and Spirit from 1977 to 1980. From 1971 to 1974 the AMX was a Javelin model and is listed on the Javelin page.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The two-seat AMX had only V8s: the 290, 343 and 390, then the 360 and 390 for 1970. Hurst built a small run of Super Stock AMXs for drag racing in 1969.
The later AMX used AMC's 258 six and 304 V8. AMC's brochures for these years print no horsepower for the six.
